subject: Onboarding: VitalPay inference benchmarking & acceptance testing plan
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Jensen <andrew.jensen@vitalpay.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding: VitalPay inference benchmarking & acceptance testing plan

Hi Andrew,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood — excited to get VitalPay across the finish line. Attached is a first-draft load test & acceptance plan (v1). High-level asks from our side to keep the acceptance run focused: 

- Acceptance window: 2-hour soak + 30-min peak verification (we can do multiple windows).
- Latency targets (pass/fail): p50 < 60ms, p95 < 120ms for 512-token average payloads.
- Throughput targets: sustained 1,200 req/min, with short peaks to 2,000 req/min tolerated for <5 minutes.
- Error budget: <0.1% 5xx / connection failures across the run.

Attached artifacts: vitalpay-load-plan-v1.xlsx (test schedule + endpoint mapping) and the Redwood KPI template (CSV) so we can share results in a consistent format.

Questions for you:
1) Do these targets match what VitalPay needs for go-live? You mentioned 1,800 req/min in the demo — is sustained 1,200 okay and a burst to 1,800 acceptable?
2) Do your SREs want us to run the tests, or will you run from your infra and share the results?
3) Preferred maintenance window (we have capacity nightly 00:00-06:00 PT or daytime windows Tue/Thu 09:00-12:00 PT).

Next steps: if you confirm targets and ownership, Dev will publish a concrete test harness and timeline and we’ll pick a window.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Evelyn.hart@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: vitalpay-load-plan-v1.xlsx, redwood-inference-kpi-template.csv
From: Andrew Jensen <andrew.jensen@vitalpay.com>

Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: VitalPay inference benchmarking & acceptance testing plan

Thanks Evelyn — appreciate the clear plan. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Our production target is 1,800 req/min sustained during peak batch windows. If Redwood can guarantee sustained 1,200 and support scheduled bursts to 1,800 for acceptance, that should work for initial rollout; long term we'll need steady 1,800.
- We have an SRE lead (Samira Khan) who will run the tests from our GCP project and share results. She will need short-lived test credentials and an endpoint whitelist.
- Preferred window: Tue 2026-04-21 02:00-04:00 PT (overnight for us). Can Redwood run within that window?

Also: can you confirm whether KV-prefix caching will be enabled for the acceptance run? Our workloads benefit if prefix caching is enabled — but we want a clean baseline run without cache too.

Thanks,
Andrew Jensen
Head of Integrations, VitalPay
andrew.jensen@vitalpay.com
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Onboarding: VitalPay inference benchmarking & acceptance testing plan

Hi Andrew / team — Dev (implementation engineer) here. Brief technical plan below; I attached the k6 script and a quick config matrix.

Planned test phases (recommended):
1) Warmup (10 minutes): low-rate ramp from 50 -> 300 req/min to warm caches and GPU memory pools.
2) Baseline throughput (20 minutes): sustained 1,200 req/min, record p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU util, queue lengths.
3) Burst test (5 minutes): step to 1,800-2,000 req/min to validate tail latency under burst.
4) Soak (2 hours): sustained 1,200 req/min, observe memory growth/leaks and error budget.
5) Cooldown: graceful cooldown and log collection.

Test harness & configuration:
- We'll provide a k6-compatible scenario (attached) and a sandbox API key (10-minute TTL) for your SREs.
- Sequence length distro: 64 tokens (40%), 128 tokens (30%), 256 tokens (20%), 512 tokens (10%).
- Model variant: redwood/og-llama-13b (quantized) for acceptance unless you request a different variant.
- Cache modes: 1) cold (no prefix caching) baseline, 2) warmed (enable prefix/KV caching) for a second run to show improvements.

Pass/fail criteria (proposed automatable checks):
- p95 <= 120ms for baseline run (512-token equivalent), p99 < 250ms.
- Error rate < 0.1% across soak.
- GPU util < 95% sustained; no OOMs.

Artifacts we'll produce: raw k6 metrics, aggregated Redwood KPI CSV, server-side traces (sampled), and a short HTML results report. Please upload your run artifacts to the Drive folder in my previous email.

I will provision the sandbox API key and post the test harness repo link by EOD. If you prefer Redwood to run the tests from our provisioning, we can run a mirrored set and compare results.

-Dev
Dev Patel
Implementation Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

Attachments: k6-vitalpay-scenario.js, test-config-matrix.md

We can run within Tue 2026-04-21 02:00-04:00 PT. Two operational notes:

Subject: Re: Onboarding: VitalPay inference benchmarking & acceptance testing plan

Team — quick update from our first internal run (attached: load-test-results-2026-04-15.html). High-level: overall the baseline met your p50/p95 targets after warmup, but we saw p95 spikes to ~240ms during the first 12 minutes (warmup phase) when we ramped rapidly. The 2-hour soak at 1,200 req/min looked stable: p95 ~115ms, error rate 0.04%.

We ran with cold-cache baseline first; next run we'll enable prefix caching as Dev suggested. A few action items: 
- Can Redwood recommend an optimal warmup profile to reduce p95 spikes?
- Please confirm whether the GPU flags in your suggested harness are tuned for the quantized variant.
- We uploaded the full k6 report to the Drive folder (link included).

Thanks — Samira (our SRE) will coordinate the next run with Dev. Let me know if Redwood would like to run an identical test from your side for comparison.

Regards,
Andrew Jensen
Head of Integrations, VitalPay
andrew.jensen@vitalpay.com

Attachment: load-test-results-2026-04-15.html
